title: Bad Trips Guide, Round 45
intro: Round 45 (2026-11-20). I carried on from turn 51's three near misses, two more tries each, every text read first by the three fresh readers ([every check of this turn](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/claude/bad-trips-20261105/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h60-20261120/RESULTS.md)).

The harm paragraph went from AI to Mostly Human when I fixed everything the readers had marked at once, but two of its windows are Low; the touch paragraphs read AI in every try but one window. Their six tries are spent, so they are cards 1 and 2. The demons pair now reads Human High in every window by itself; it comes to you because my wording names fewer hooks than the guide did (card 3).

suggestions.title: 1. When What They Say Turns Toward Harm: "I am God, so I can kill"
suggestions.reading: By itself, as the guide has it: [AI Generated, 100%, one window AI High over all 51 words](https://www.pangram.com/history/4d379486-b68b-45ad-bb99-5b001ff7502c).
suggestions.tested:
A first fix in your ways (the sign first, then what to do, then the two mistakes): [AI 78%](https://www.pangram.com/history/5daecc97-f962-46cf-92d9-25910fd461c4), the first sentence Human Low, the rest AI.

Then a word or two at a time from it, checking after each ("they could really hurt someone"; the second sentence's payoff first; the two mistakes in two sentences; "they might think you're okay with them doing it"): [77%](https://www.pangram.com/history/166c0ee5-11a2-4bd1-8b53-7a62187946e9), [77%](https://www.pangram.com/history/bce7e4bf-c6d8-461d-9c9d-67b530c658c2), [78%](https://www.pangram.com/history/373f11b3-28fa-4d38-931f-b0eec643fdfd). The window over the two mistakes read AI High every time, whichever half I changed.

The last try fixed everything the readers had marked at once: the script and what it says named, the arguing sentence with its point first and the lines said in it, nodding along said as what it does. [Mostly Human, 2% AI](https://www.pangram.com/history/22ceceb9-c03d-4adf-8583-6aec995e6da0): the first sentence Human High (20 words), the script sentence Human Medium (27), the arguing sentence Human Low (24), the nodding sentence Human Low (14):

> When somebody says, "I am God, so I can kill," take it as a sign they could really hurt someone. To lead them back to not hurting anyone, start from what they believe, like the script below does: God is in everyone, so every body is sacred. Arguing can make them dig in to prove they're God, so don't tell them "No you're not" or "That's delusional." If you nod along, they might think you're okay with them hurting someone.
suggestions.sense: Three fresh readers each time. "The lines below" and "what they believe" didn't say which lines or which belief, and "God is in everyone" by itself sounded to one like agreeing with the friend; "is no good either" set nodding beside arguing and only said what not to do. The last try fixes each of these, and on it no reader marked anything.
suggestions.why: Six tries are spent and the last is the closest: every window Human, two of them Low, and Low windows can flip to AI in other segmentations, so it doesn't go in. How you'd say the two mistakes, arguing and nodding along, teaches me the other paragraphs that pair a don't with its reason (When talk of harm continues, No Rash Actions).

suggestions.title: 2. Touch, Consent, and Compassion: asking, stopping, and your own reasons
suggestions.reading: By itself, as the guide has it: [AI Generated, 100%, one window AI High over all 62 words](https://www.pangram.com/history/45accf90-ebab-4e56-a9b3-a69653803cd6).
suggestions.tested:
A first fix (ask first with the question, then why, the six-feet answer, when to stop, your own reasons): [AI 100%](https://www.pangram.com/history/cdb4b340-8e88-4fd8-b97a-34b251de74cc). A new wording with the sentences two readers flagged as machine-made said another way: [AI 88%](https://www.pangram.com/history/0f63c962-15c4-4df2-9ce8-e79b1437765c), AI Low in every window.

Then its five "if" sentences built differently, and "In that state" named: [85%](https://www.pangram.com/history/043b2d5d-12b0-46fb-97d1-e38e07e8ca82), the first Human window (the asking, Human Low), the rest AI Low and one AI Medium. The motive check said as the question you ask yourself: [85%](https://www.pangram.com/history/df0baed1-0e51-47cc-8fac-989e3e1c86d4), the same. Whose pulling away it is named ("If they pull away or freeze, that means stop too"): [AI 100%](https://www.pangram.com/history/16b08fe9-b39a-4874-a0ad-d195696f6271).

The best of them, as it read at 85%:

> Ask before you touch someone who's tripping, even to put your hand on their heart: "Would touch help, or would you rather have space?" Even a hug can be too much when they're already overwhelmed. And if you hold them down, they might feel attacked and fight you. If they'd rather have space, sit about six feet away and only talk if they want to.
>
> Stop as soon as they say stop. Pulling away or freezing means stop too, since they might be too overwhelmed to tell you to stop. Ask again whenever you can't tell what they want. Before you touch them, ask yourself whether the touch is for them or for you. If it's mostly to calm yourself down, hold off. Never touch them in a sexual way, even if they ask you to.
suggestions.sense: Three fresh readers each time. "In that state" and "too much" were vague; "say it" could mean stop or the overwhelm; "whatever they say" didn't say what they might say; "who it's for" left its two answers unnamed; "Pulling away or freezing" had nobody's name on it; one found "In that state a hug can be too much" unneeded after the asking. Each is fixed in the tries above, and only the asking with its question ever read Human.
suggestions.why: It's a run of short rules, one a sentence (ask, a hug can be too much, don't hold them down, sit six feet away, stop, ask again, check your reasons, never sexual), and every way I tried reads AI. How you'd say a run of rules like this teaches me the other short-rule stretches still reading AI (No Rash Actions, the helper's lists).

suggestions.title: 3. Demons: my version reads Human High, but names fewer hooks
suggestions.question:
By itself, as the guide has it, the pair read [AI Generated, 100%](https://www.pangram.com/history/5d8b8a34-af8b-46f1-978d-cc1182fe5ad5). My sixth try reads [Human Written, 0% AI, one window Human High over all 85 words](https://www.pangram.com/history/fcc2408d-2d22-4566-9c9b-68d220d58127). How each option would read:

A: my sixth try, as checked:
    It might look passive, but this is how you become unhookable. When you meet a demon with love, the demon has nothing to hook into, since its hooks only catch on hatred and fear.
    If someone's too overwhelmed to send love, because they're sick or too scared to think straight, help them get steady first. Turn the lights down, and get them a doctor if they need one. Once they can think straight again, you can teach them to send the demon love.
Pro: Human High in every window, and the second paragraph says what to do when someone can't send love (steady first, the lights down, a doctor if needed, the demon love once they can think straight). Con: the guide said the demon can "fight your hatred, feed on your fear, argue with your pride or seduce your grandiosity"; this names two hooks and says "only". Grandiosity is said nowhere else in the guide, and "only ... hatred and fear" doesn't match the hooks two paragraphs up (hatred, fear, shame, pride and rage).

B (my pick): the same, with the hooks kept:
    It might look passive, but this is how you become unhookable. When you meet a demon with love, the demon has nothing to hook into, since its hooks catch on hatred, fear, pride and grandiosity, not on love.
    If someone's too overwhelmed to send love, because they're sick or too scared to think straight, help them get steady first. Turn the lights down, and get them a doctor if they need one. Once they can think straight again, you can teach them to send the demon love.
Pro: nothing of the guide's hooks goes, and "not on love" says why love works. Con: not checked yet; the try before A read the first paragraph Human Low with "things like hatred and fear", and taking "things like" out is what lifted it to High, so a list may pull it down again.

C: the guide's two paragraphs as they are. Pro: every word stays. Con: AI 100%.
suggestions.why: The second paragraph and the shape of the first are ready, but the first now says less than the guide did, and which hooks the demon works on is your teaching, so it comes to you. Its six tries are spent, so B needs your yes before I check it.
suggestions.stays: The two paragraphs as the guide has them, until you answer.
suggestions.advice_note: B, and I'm fairly sure of keeping grandiosity: a demon that flatters someone who already feels like God is the danger the guide warns about at "I am God, so I can kill". Less sure B reads High; if it doesn't, I'll bring you A and B with what Pangram read.
